structures.text: The cerebral hemispheres form the largest part of the brain.
bullets: Five lobes in the lecture: frontal, parietal, temporal, occipital and insula.
Three surfaces: superolateral, medial and inferior.

structures.name: Brainstem
structures.text: The brainstem is one of the three brain components named in this lecture.
bullets: Shown in its source position below the cerebrum.
Cerebrum, brainstem and cerebellum together form the brain.

structures.name: Cerebellum
structures.text: The cerebellum lies behind the brainstem and below the posterior cerebrum.

structures.name: Spinal cord
structures.text: The spinal cord and brain make up the central nervous system.

structures.name: Peripheral nerves
structures.text: The PNS includes nerves branching from the brain and spinal cord.
bullets: Cranial nerves leave the brain; spinal nerves connect with the spinal cord.
The model shows selected actual nerves and spinal roots as examples.

structures.name: Grey matter
structures.text: Grey matter consists mainly of neuronal cell bodies.
bullets: The outer cerebral cortex is grey matter.
A CNS collection of neuronal cell bodies is called a nucleus.

structures.name: White matter
structures.text: White matter contains predominantly myelinated axons.
bullets: Deep cerebral white matter links cortical and subcortical regions.
Association, commissural and projection fibers are studied at the end of the lecture.

structures.name: Nucleus
structures.text: A nucleus is a collection of neuronal cell bodies within the CNS.
bullets: The caudate nucleus is shown as a location example, not an additional examinable nucleus list.

structures.name: Ganglion
structures.text: A ganglion is a collection of neuronal cell bodies outside the CNS.
bullets: Compare its position on a spinal nerve with the CNS nucleus.

structures.name: Frontal lobe
meshes: Opercular part of inferior frontal gyrus.l
Opercular part of inferior frontal gyrus.r
Orbital part of  inferior frontal gyrus.l
Orbital part of  inferior frontal gyrus.r
Triangular part of inferior frontal gyrus.l
Triangular part of inferior frontal gyrus.r
structures.text: Anterior to the central sulcus and above the lateral sulcus.
bullets: Contains the precentral gyrus and superior, middle and inferior frontal gyri.
structures.clarification: Lobe colors follow the original segmented anatomical parcels. Functional borders are not inferred from these colors.

structures.name: Parietal lobe
structures.text: Posterior to the central sulcus and above the lateral sulcus.
bullets: Includes postcentral gyrus, superior parietal lobule and inferior parietal lobule.
structures.clarification: Lobe colors follow the original segmented anatomical parcels. Functional borders are not inferred from these colors.

structures.name: Temporal lobe
structures.text: Below the lateral sulcus.
bullets: Identify the superior, middle and inferior temporal gyri.
structures.clarification: Lobe colors follow the original segmented anatomical parcels. Functional borders are not inferred from these colors.

structures.name: Occipital lobe
structures.text: The posterior lobe, related to vision.
bullets: Its lateral border is a conventional line, not a single continuous sulcus.
structures.clarification: Lobe colors follow the original segmented anatomical parcels. Functional borders are not inferred from these colors.

structures.name: Insula · circular boundary
structures.text: The insula lies in the depth of the lateral sulcus, under the opercula.
bullets: The highlighted circular sulcus marks its deep boundary. Surrounding opercula are removed from this view.
Lecture functions: visceral sensation, equilibrium-related input and taste.
structures.clarification: The exported “Insula (Subcentral gyrus and ant. and post. sulci*)” object is a combined surface parcel, not a reliable isolated insular cortex. It is not used as an insular fill. The genuine circular sulcus locates the boundary; no unsegmented insular gyri are invented.

structures.name: Central sulcus
structures.text: Separates the frontal and parietal lobes.
bullets: Precentral gyrus is anterior; postcentral gyrus is posterior.
Rolando is the lecture eponym.

structures.name: Lateral sulcus
structures.text: Separates temporal cortex below from frontal and parietal cortex above.
bullets: Sylvius is the lecture eponym.
The insula is deeper than the visible lips of this fissure.

structures.name: Parieto-occipital sulcus
structures.text: A key boundary between parietal and occipital cortex on the medial surface.
bullets: On the lateral surface, the occipital boundary continues as a conventional line to the preoccipital notch.

structures.name: Precentral gyrus · BA 4
structures.text: Primary motor cortex: voluntary motor control of the opposite side of the body.
bullets: Medial representation: genitalia, hip, leg, foot and toes; ACA supply.
Lateral representation: head, neck, upper limb and face; MCA supply.
A lesion can produce contralateral hemiplegia.

structures.name: Precentral sulcus
structures.text: Forms the anterior border of the precentral gyrus.
bullets: The central sulcus forms its posterior border.

structures.name: Frontal sulci
structures.text: Superior and inferior frontal sulci separate the three frontal gyri.
bullets: Superior frontal gyrus: above the superior frontal sulcus.
Middle frontal gyrus: between the two sulci.
Inferior frontal gyrus: below the inferior frontal sulcus.

structures.name: Superior frontal gyrus
structures.text: The upper frontal gyrus continues onto the medial surface.
bullets: Use the medial view to follow its medial frontal continuation.

structures.name: Middle frontal gyrus
structures.text: The middle frontal gyrus lies between the superior and inferior frontal sulci.

structures.name: Inferior frontal gyrus
meshes: Opercular part of inferior frontal gyrus.l
Opercular part of inferior frontal gyrus.r
Orbital part of  inferior frontal gyrus.l
Orbital part of  inferior frontal gyrus.r
Triangular part of inferior frontal gyrus.l
Triangular part of inferior frontal gyrus.r
structures.text: Its named parts are pars opercularis, pars triangularis and pars orbitalis.
bullets: Broca’s classical BA 44/45 territory is associated with the opercular and triangular parts of the dominant hemisphere.
structures.clarification: The slide repeats an orbital label. Pars opercularis is the missing third anatomical name; pars orbitalis is not classically part of BA 44/45.

structures.name: Broca’s area · BA 44/45
meshes: Opercular part of inferior frontal gyrus.l
Opercular part of inferior frontal gyrus.r
Triangular part of inferior frontal gyrus.l
Triangular part of inferior frontal gyrus.r
structures.text: Motor speech production in the language-dominant hemisphere.
bullets: Classical lesion pattern: nonfluent, effortful expressive aphasia.
Comprehension is relatively better preserved than speech output.
The left hemisphere is shown as the usual language-dominant example.
structures.clarification: This is a classical regional locator on the opercular/triangular gyri, not a subject-specific cytoarchitectonic BA 44/45 map.

structures.name: Premotor & supplementary cortex · BA 6
structures.text: Plans, sequences and helps organize movement.
bullets: Located anterior to primary motor cortex.
Supplementary motor cortex occupies the medial frontal region.
structures.clarification: The highlighted gyri are location context. This source has no independent BA 6 segmentation, so their entire outline is not a BA 6 boundary.

structures.name: Prefrontal cortex
structures.text: Frontal association cortex supports executive and behavioral functions.
bullets: Personality and behavior.
Working memory and cognition.
Decision making and motor planning.
structures.clarification: Frontal source parcels identify the region; they do not define an exact functional border.

structures.name: Frontal eye field · BA 8
structures.text: Controls conjugate voluntary eye movements.
bullets: A destructive unilateral lesion may cause the eyes to deviate toward the lesion.
Locate it in the frontal region anterior to the motor strip.
structures.clarification: Only a regional locator is available. The source does not contain an exact BA 8 mesh.

structures.name: Postcentral gyrus · BA 3,1,2
structures.text: Primary somatosensory cortex: receives sensory information from the opposite body side.
bullets: Medial representation: genitalia, hip, leg, foot and toes; ACA supply.
Lateral representation: head, neck, upper limb and face; MCA supply.
A lesion may produce contralateral hemi-hypoesthesia.

structures.name: Postcentral sulcus
structures.text: Forms the posterior boundary of the postcentral gyrus.

structures.name: Intraparietal sulcus
structures.text: Separates superior and inferior parietal lobules.

structures.name: Superior parietal lobule
structures.text: Parietal cortex superior to the intraparietal sulcus.

structures.name: Inferior parietal lobule
structures.text: Comprises supramarginal and angular gyri.
bullets: Supramarginal gyrus caps the posterior lateral fissure.
Angular gyrus lies around the posterior end of the superior temporal sulcus.

structures.name: Supramarginal gyrus · BA 40
structures.text: The anterior part of the inferior parietal lobule, wrapping the end of the lateral sulcus.

structures.name: Angular gyrus · BA 39
structures.text: The posterior part of the inferior parietal lobule.
bullets: Use the end of the superior temporal sulcus as its landmark.

structures.name: Somatosensory association cortex
structures.text: Interprets tactile features, spatial position, size and learned sensory meaning.
bullets: Astereognosis: inability to recognize an object by touch.
Agraphesthesia: inability to recognize a traced symbol.
Impaired position/body-part recognition is listed in the lecture as “Astatagnosis”.
Abarognosis: impaired discrimination of weight.
structures.clarification: The slide calls the deficit “Graphesthesia”; graphesthesia is the ability, while agraphesthesia is its loss. Functional coverage is broader than a single source parcel.

structures.name: Wernicke’s language region
structures.text: A posterior temporal–parietal language network supports comprehension.
bullets: Lecture emphasis: BA 39 and 40, interpretation of spoken and written words.
Classical lesion pattern: fluent but poorly meaningful speech with impaired comprehension.
structures.clarification: BA 39/40 alone are not a complete modern definition. Posterior temporal cortex is also important; the colored gyri are regional context, not an exact Wernicke boundary.

structures.name: Temporal sulci
structures.text: The two sulci separate the superior, middle and inferior temporal gyri.

structures.name: Temporal gyri
structures.text: Three stacked gyri occupy the lateral temporal surface.
bullets: Superior temporal gyrus below the lateral fissure.
Middle temporal gyrus between the temporal sulci.
Inferior temporal gyrus below the inferior temporal sulcus.

structures.name: Primary auditory cortex · BA 41/42
structures.text: Perception and awareness of sound.
bullets: The transverse temporal gyri lie on the superior temporal surface, hidden inside the lateral fissure.
The lecture describes contralateral sound-stimulus loss.
structures.clarification: Auditory input reaches both hemispheres. A unilateral cortical lesion does not usually produce complete deafness in the opposite ear; severe cortical deafness generally requires bilateral damage.

structures.name: Auditory association cortex
structures.text: Analyzes and recognizes the meaning of sound and perceived words.
structures.clarification: The source gyri show location context, not an exact functional parcellation.

structures.name: Olfactory cortex
structures.text: Primary olfactory regions support awareness of smell; association regions support recognition and smell memory.
structures.clarification: The source combines parahippocampal anatomy and does not isolate the uncus or an olfactory functional area. Pins identify the related region, not an exact olfactory boundary.

structures.name: Occipital sulci & gyri
structures.text: Locate the occipital gyri and the lunate / lateral occipital landmarks.
bullets: Superior and inferior occipital gyri are named in the lecture.
Sulcal shape and the lunate landmark vary between individuals.
structures.clarification: The lecture’s lateral occipital sulcus has no exact standalone mesh in this export. Its parent occipital parcels and original slide provide the reference.

structures.name: Primary visual cortex · BA 17
structures.text: Awareness of visual stimuli is associated with cortex around the calcarine sulcus.
bullets: A lesion can cause visual-field impairment.
The lecture links the occipital lobe to vision.
structures.clarification: The calcarine landmark and adjacent gyri are shown. Their full outlines are not an exact BA 17 boundary.

structures.name: Visual association cortex · BA 18/19
structures.text: Analyzes and recognizes visual stimuli and their meaning.
bullets: Visual agnosia is a failure of visual recognition, rather than simple loss of visual detection.
structures.clarification: This is an occipital regional locator; source parcels are not exact BA 18/19 maps.

structures.name: Cingulate gyrus
meshes: Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Middle anterior part).l
Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Middle anterior part).r
Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Middle posterior part).l
Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Middle posterior part).r
Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Posterior dorsal part).l
Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Posterior dorsal part).r
structures.text: The lecture links this limbic-system region with emotion.
bullets: Follow its arch above the corpus callosum.
The cingulate and callosal sulci are its key medial landmarks.
structures.clarification: Some source parcels combine cingulate gyrus and sulcus. The names and parcel limits are retained rather than split by invented geometry.

structures.name: Callosal & cingulate sulci
meshes: Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Middle anterior part).l
Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Middle anterior part).r
Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Middle posterior part).l
Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Middle posterior part).r
Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Posterior dorsal part).l
Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Posterior dorsal part).r
structures.text: The callosal sulcus lies between the corpus callosum and cingulate gyrus; the cingulate sulcus is above the gyrus.
structures.clarification: The callosal sulcus is a gap between the real meshes, not an independent source object. This is a relation view, not a falsely labeled sulcus mesh.

structures.name: Medial frontal gyrus
structures.text: Follow the medial continuation of the superior frontal gyrus.

structures.name: Paracentral lobule
structures.text: The medial continuation around the terminal central sulcus.
bullets: The lecture emphasizes control related to micturition and defecation.
Motor and sensory lower-limb representation also reaches this medial region.
structures.clarification: The source parcel combines paracentral gyrus and sulcus. The lobule spans frontal and parietal cortex; its complete source outline is shown in a separate color rather than assigned entirely to one lobe.

structures.name: Y-shaped medial sulci
structures.text: The lecture’s Y is formed by parieto-occipital, pre-calcarine and post-calcarine components.
bullets: Identify the parieto-occipital limb and the calcarine course.
Use the original figure to distinguish the pre- and post-calcarine terminology.
structures.clarification: The source contains one continuous calcarine mesh. Its subdivisions are not separate geometry.

structures.name: Cuneus
structures.text: The wedge of medial occipital cortex above the calcarine sulcus.

structures.name: Precuneus
structures.text: Medial parietal cortex anterior to the parieto-occipital sulcus.

structures.name: Orbital surface
structures.text: The anterior part of the inferior cerebral surface rests above the orbits.
bullets: Find the olfactory sulcus and gyrus rectus.
The orbital sulci form an H-shaped arrangement.
Anterior, posterior, medial and lateral orbital gyri are listed in the lecture.
structures.clarification: The four orbital gyri share the original “Orbital gyri” object. Individual sub-gyri are not fabricated or given false hard borders.

structures.name: Olfactory sulcus
structures.text: Separates gyrus rectus medially from orbital gyri laterally.

structures.name: H-shaped orbital sulci
structures.text: The H-shaped arrangement divides the orbital gyri.

structures.name: Gyrus rectus
structures.text: The straight gyrus along the medial orbital surface, medial to the olfactory sulcus.

structures.name: Tentorial surface
structures.text: The posterior part of the inferior surface includes temporal and occipital structures.
bullets: Rhinal sulcus and uncus are named on the original slide.
Collateral sulcus separates parahippocampal from occipitotemporal anatomy.
Find lingual gyrus and medial/lateral occipitotemporal gyri.
structures.clarification: Rhinal sulcus and uncus are not independently segmented here. They are taught from the original figure and their related parahippocampal source parcel, with no invented mesh labels.

structures.name: Collateral sulcus
structures.text: A key inferior-surface groove beside the parahippocampal and occipitotemporal regions.

structures.name: Lingual gyrus
structures.text: Inferomedial occipital gyrus below the calcarine sulcus.

structures.name: Occipitotemporal gyri
structures.text: Compare the medial and lateral occipitotemporal regions and their separating sulcus.
structures.clarification: “Medial occipitotemporal” and parahippocampal terminology overlap in this source’s combined parcel. See the original lecture labels for the course terminology.

structures.name: Taste / gustatory region
meshes: Opercular part of inferior frontal gyrus.l
Opercular part of inferior frontal gyrus.r
structures.text: The lecture’s sensory summary places taste near the base of the postcentral region and also lists taste under insular function.
bullets: Relate the insular and opercular region to the lateral sulcus.
structures.clarification: The circular sulcus and adjacent opercular region are anatomical context. No exact gustatory functional territory is independently segmented in this source.

structures.name: Association fibers
structures.text: Connect areas within the same cerebral hemisphere.
bullets: Short association fibers link adjacent gyri.
Long association fibers link more widely separated gyri or lobes.

structures.name: Commissural fibers
structures.text: Connect cortical regions across the two hemispheres.
bullets: The corpus callosum is the largest commissure.
Other lecture examples: anterior, posterior, habenular and fornix commissures.

structures.name: Projection fibers
structures.text: Ascending and descending fibers connect cortex with lower CNS structures.
bullets: They pass to or from the cerebral cortex.
Compare “within one hemisphere”, “between hemispheres” and “toward lower centers”.

structures.name: Corpus callosum
structures.text: The largest commissural connection between the cerebral hemispheres.
bullets: Parts listed in the lecture: rostrum, genu, body and splenium.
Use the medial original figure to follow these parts from anterior to posterior.
structures.clarification: The source provides a single corpus-callosum mesh. Part names are anchored to its real surface; artificial cut boundaries are not presented as separately segmented anatomy.

structures.name: Anterior commissure
structures.text: One of the commissural-fiber examples named in the lecture.

structures.name: Posterior commissure
structures.text: The posterior commissure lies inferior to the pineal region in the lecture diagram.
structures.clarification: The pineal gland is not present in the selected source model. The relationship is shown on the original lecture figure, not by labeling a different structure as pineal.

structures.name: Habenular commissure · relation
structures.text: The lecture places the habenular commissure superior to the pineal region.
structures.clarification: The highlighted parent structure is the habenula. No standalone habenular-commissure mesh is available; the original lecture figure gives the exact relation.

structures.name: Commissure of fornix
structures.text: The hippocampal commissure is the source object corresponding to the lecture’s fornix commissure.

quiz.prompt: Which sulcus separates frontal and parietal lobes?
quiz.explanation: The central sulcus lies between precentral and postcentral gyri.

quiz.prompt: Which gyrus contains primary motor cortex?
quiz.explanation: Precentral gyrus is the lecture’s BA 4 motor strip.

quiz.prompt: Which gyrus contains primary somatosensory cortex?
quiz.explanation: Postcentral gyrus corresponds to BA 3, 1 and 2.

quiz.prompt: Which hidden lobe lies in the lateral fissure?
quiz.explanation: The insula is concealed by the surrounding opercula.

quiz.prompt: Which region is classically associated with expressive aphasia?
quiz.explanation: Broca’s dominant frontal region supports speech production.

quiz.prompt: Which region is associated with receptive aphasia in the lecture?
quiz.explanation: The posterior language network supports comprehension.

quiz.prompt: Which sulcus divides superior and inferior parietal lobules?
quiz.explanation: The intraparietal sulcus separates the two parietal lobules.

quiz.prompt: Which gyrus is labeled BA 40?
quiz.explanation: Supramarginal is BA 40; angular is BA 39.

quiz.prompt: Which gyrus is labeled BA 39?
quiz.explanation: Angular gyrus is the lecture’s BA 39.

quiz.prompt: What is the largest commissure?
quiz.explanation: The corpus callosum is the largest commissural structure.

quiz.prompt: Which fibers connect areas within one hemisphere?
quiz.explanation: Short and long association fibers remain within one hemisphere.

quiz.prompt: Which fibers pass toward or from lower CNS structures?
quiz.explanation: Projection fibers carry ascending and descending cortical connections.

quiz.prompt: Which region is a collection of cell bodies inside the CNS?
quiz.explanation: Nucleus is the CNS term; ganglion is outside the CNS.

quiz.prompt: Which lobe is primarily associated with vision in this lecture?
quiz.explanation: Occipital cortex includes primary and association visual regions.

quiz.prompt: Which gyri contain primary auditory cortex?
quiz.explanation: Transverse temporal gyri are the anatomical auditory landmark.

quiz.prompt: Which inferior groove lies lateral to gyrus rectus?
quiz.explanation: The olfactory sulcus separates gyrus rectus from orbital gyri.

quiz.prompt: Which cortex is associated with emotions in the lecture?
quiz.explanation: The cingulate gyrus belongs to the limbic region.

quiz.prompt: Which medial region is linked to micturition and defecation?
quiz.explanation: The lecture emphasizes these functions at the paracentral lobule.

quiz.prompt: Which frontal region is associated with conjugate gaze?
quiz.explanation: The lecture assigns conjugate eye movement to BA 8.

quiz.prompt: What connects opposite cerebral hemispheres?
quiz.explanation: Commissural fibers cross between hemispheres.
